title: Rahab becomes part of God’s people — Joshua 6
paragraphs: Rahab becomes part of God’s people — Joshua 6
She was supposed to be destroyed with the city.
But grace put a scarlet thread on her window.

Rahab was a Canaanite. A prostitute. A woman from a city marked for judgment.
And yet when Jericho fell, she did not fall with it. Joshua 6 says she and her family were spared, and she “lives in Israel to this day” because she hid the spies Joshua sent (Joshua 6:25).

Rahab was not an insider trying to get back on track.
She was an outsider brought all the way in.
That is the kind of God we are dealing with.

A God who tears down walls but saves the one house marked by faith.
A God who judges sin without failing to honor repentance.
A God who can pull a woman out of a cursed city and write her into the story of His people.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Rahab believed the God of Israel was the true God before she ever stood among Israel. She bet her life on His mercy. She tied the scarlet cord in her window, and that cord became more than a sign of rescue. It became a whisper of the Gospel. Because all through Scripture, God saves people not by pedigree, not by performance, but by faith in His promise.

Rahab’s past said unclean.
God’s grace said come in.

Her city said condemned.
God’s mercy said spared.

Her name could have ended in shame.
Instead, by grace, it ends in belonging.

And beloved, that is the Gospel of Jesus Christ. We were outsiders. Guilty. Cut off. Deserving judgment. But through Christ, God brings the far-off near. By His blood, sinners become sons and daughters. The rejected are received. The stained are washed. The lost are brought into the household of God.

Rahab did not clean herself up and then get chosen.
She believed.
And God saved her.
So if the enemy keeps telling you, “You don’t belong with God’s people,” remember Rahab standing alive while Jericho burned behind her.

Grace can bring you out.
Grace can bring you in.
Grace can rewrite everything.
Jesus still receives the ones shame counted out.
